title: Temple Tax
summary: Temple Tax is a cultic institution rooted in Israel's worship life, organizing presence, holiness, mediation, and sacrifice.
historical_context: Temple Tax develops from wilderness worship into temple-centered practice and later second-temple memory.
ancient_near_east_context: Ancient temples and sacrificial systems provide the wider background, but Israel gives them covenant shape.
literary_context: The Pentateuch, Psalms, Prophets, Gospels, Hebrews, and Revelation all use Temple Tax language.
covenantal_significance: Temple Tax gives concrete form to divine presence among a holy people.
interpretive_notes: Cultic institutions are about worship and mediated access, not just ritual detail.
New Testament writers often reinterpret these institutions around Christ.
common_questions: How does this institution shape worship?
